test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Under which article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Equality guaranteed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14 to Article 18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Equality** is guaranteed under **Articles 14 to 18** of the Indian Constitution. It is one of the fundamental rights provided to citizens of India.
 
• **Article 14:** Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This ensures no discrimination against individuals on any grounds.
 
• **Article 15:** Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. It also enables the state to make special provisions for women, children, and socially disadvantaged groups.
 
• **Article 16:** Ensures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. It prohibits discrimination in employment based on religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence.
 
• **Article 17:** Abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form. This article is a step towards eradicating caste-based discrimination in society.
 
• **Article 18:** Abolishes titles except for military and academic distinctions. It aims to prevent the creation of artificial hierarchies in Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, providing citizens with basic human rights essential for their development.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, ensuring protection against arbitrary actions by the state.
 
• They include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• **Article 14:**
 
 
• It emphasizes equality before the law, ensuring that every individual is subject to the same laws without favoritism.
 
• The concept of "equal protection of the laws" guarantees that individuals in similar circumstances will be treated equally.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:**
 
 
• It prohibits discrimination on specific grounds, fostering inclusivity and social justice.
 
• The state is empowered to make affirmative actions like reservations for disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Article 17:**
 
 
• This article is instrumental in abolishing untouchability, a social evil prevalent in India.
 
• It ensures that individuals belonging to the lower castes are treated equally and with dignity.
 
 
 
• **Article 18:**
 
 
• It prevents individuals from using titles that create social hierarchies, ensuring a classless society.
 
• Military and academic distinctions are exceptions under this article.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights vs Directive Principles:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by courts, while Directive Principles of State Policy are non-enforceable guidelines for governance.
 
• Both aim to establish a welfare state but differ in their legal binding nature.
 
 
 
• **Equality vs Equity:**
 
 
• Equality ensures equal treatment for all, while equity focuses on fairness and addressing disparities.
 
• Articles 15 and 16 incorporate elements of equity through affirmative actions like reservations.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in interpreting and safeguarding fundamental rights.
 
• Landmark cases like Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala reaffirm the importance of fundamental rights in India's constitutional framework.
